subject: Risk & Compliance
title: De-Risking and Financial Exclusion
description: A quick win: understand De-Risking and Financial Exclusion.

hook.text: Banks are so afraid of AML fines that they close accounts for entire countries and communities.

buildup.text: De-risking means cutting off high-risk customers or regions entirely rather than managing the risk.

discovery.text: Caribbean and African nations lost access to US banking because global banks found compliance too expensive.

twist.text: De-risking pushes people toward informal channels — exactly the unmonitored systems AML tries to prevent.

climax.text: AML rules meant to stop crime are accidentally excluding entire populations from the financial system.

punchline.text: Too risky to bank. Cut them off. Crime moves underground.

quiz.question: What is the unintended consequence of de-risking?
options: It pushes people toward unmonitored informal channels
